title: Shite and onions!
html_source:
What stinks? Shite and onions!

Shite carries a long history, intertwined somewhat with that of shit on account of the older phonetic forms of the latter. The Oxford English Dictionary, has citations from Larkin, Enright, Hemingway, Amis, and (inevitably and repeatedly) Joyce.

Shite often functions as a standalone expletive to express irritation, regret, and other moderately negative states, quite often tempered by wry amusement or ironic detachment…shite is much more expressive and usually a bit milder than shit.

from Shite-talk and gobshites in Irish English
Stan Carey January 6, 2015
